variants.name: Anatomical woodcut
variants.description: Ivory paper, carved black shadow, precise anatomical hatching, one blood-red ink.
variants.style: The entire world is a haunting anatomical woodcut / copper engraving come to life. Warm ivory paper-white lights, vast deliberate solid black shadow shapes, and restrained dark vermilion as the sole saturated color on the existing red seams and weapon energy. Fine etched contour and crosshatching follow each object's volume in 3D; density describes form rather than a uniform screen overlay. Bone arches look engraved, floor has spare ruled perspective lines, distant forms simplify. Horned enemies have clear carved anatomical muscle and pale picked-out skeletal edges. The gun has intricate engraved bone and woodgrain leather. Strong graphic composition, museum-quality antique print craft, no sepia photographic realism, no halftone comic dots.

variants.name: Wax & wire
variants.description: Handmade wax, plaster, stitched leather and exposed armatures under practical light.
variants.style: A meticulously handmade practical stop-motion horror set viewed from first person at life size. Grubby beeswax and sculpted plaster bone arches with tiny fingerprints, uneven handmade edges, worn soot-dark painted wood and riveted metal wall panels. The two horned enemies are disturbing detailed wax-and-wire puppets, taut stitched skin, subtle exposed armature at joints, asymmetric sculpted faces. Skull gun is a tangible crafted prop of aged waxy bone, leather stitching and oxidized brass, arm is frayed fabric and sculpted material. Warm amber practical lamps, cold dusty fill, olive-gray shadows, muted dried-blood accents. Physically tangible tactile surface detail with believable miniature-craft shadows but NO toy-scale tilt-shift or blurred gameplay. NOT cute, not plastic CGI, no generic photoreal zombies. Keep the existing broad shapes and empty space.

variants.name: Decaying fresco
variants.description: Chalk pigment, cracked plaster, bruised violet and fragments of tarnished gold.
variants.style: A decaying sacred fresco made into a fully navigable first-person world. Chalky matte pigments, oxidized gold leaf, faded bone whites, dried oxblood, bruised violet and dusty blue shadow. Visible hand-painted brush structure follows the 3D surfaces; genuine worn plaster, fine cracks and patches of earlier painted layers appear ON existing walls and arches. On the existing wall masses only, subtle barely visible erased devotional figures are part of the paint, not additional characters or geometry. Elongated mournful horned creatures rendered as weathered painted icons, recognizable original pose and size. The skull weapon reads as a tarnished ceremonial reliquary with pigment-worn bone and gold details. Luminous gentle chiaroscuro, restrained atmospheric depth. A rich painterly image with a clear FPS scene, not an image of a painting hung on a wall, not photorealistic PBR, not an ornate new cathedral.

variants.name: Porcelain anatomy
variants.description: Milk-white ceramic, surgical green enamel, black rubber and precise crimson seams.
variants.style: Clinical porcelain anatomical horror. Transform existing bone arches and rib structure into milk-white glazed ceramic with fine deliberate seam lines and hairline cracks. Existing wall panels and tiled floor become aged surgical mint / celadon enamel, dark desaturated green gaps and matte black rubber trim. The two horned enemies are unsettling articulated porcelain anatomical teaching models, glazed ivory faces and torsos, dark joint sockets, fine numbered-looking gold tick marks with NO actual readable text, tiny controlled deep crimson glimpses along anatomical seams. Retain original creatures' silhouette, horns, size and placement. Skull gun becomes beautifully manufactured ceramic, black rubber and surgical steel, bandaged sleeve becomes pale clinical cloth. Bright cold examination lighting and soft green ambient light, clearly visible spaces, ominous cleanliness. Sophisticated believable stylized 3D materials, no cartoon outlines, no excessive blood, no newly invented medical furniture.

variants.name: Haunted photocopy
variants.description: Distressed black toner, coarse halftones and misregistered red technical printing.
variants.style: A haunted industrial service manual rendered as an immersive 3D FPS. Very high contrast black toner and dirty off-white paper, restrained signal-red second printing layer. Coarse purposeful halftone shading and photocopier edge breakup on surfaces, technical diagram linework following the real geometry, localized red misregistration on existing warning accents. Wall panels show faint schematic fragments only as texture, no readable type. Enemies look like anatomical illustrations assembled into horned humanoids from slightly incompatible paper diagrams, creepy rigid dark silhouettes with white diagram detail. Skull gun rendered in intricate technical cutaway-like line work WITHOUT changing its outline. Graphic brutal industrial print aesthetic, distinct from antique woodcut: mechanically reproduced halftone, hard stencil shapes, cropped diagrams, toner voids and offset printing. Keep surface noise controlled and central gameplay lane readable. No full-screen scanline overlay, no fake screenshot border.

variants.name: Living charcoal
variants.description: Directional charcoal, erased edges, ash-gray atmosphere and a few warm embers.
variants.style: A living charcoal drawing in three-dimensional space. Rich velvety compressed charcoal blacks, ash-gray midtones, chalk highlights on edges, directional hand-drawn marks wrapping around each existing surface. Walls rubbed and erased with soft incomplete outer edges, large simplified shadow masses, atmospheric depth with clear central arches. Two horned enemies seem drawn with nervous deliberate strokes, pale contour edges emerging from black masses, faint localized erased after-contours near their hands only. The bone gun has the finest sharp charcoal modeling in the foreground, bandages drawn in chalk with visible paper tooth. Restrained tiny warm ember-orange on existing weapon light and floor seams, otherwise nearly monochrome cool gray. Beautiful eerie authored drawing, not a generic pencil sketch filter or blurry scene. Keep enemies, gun, floor perspective and architecture recognizable, no extra monsters, no new objects, no heavy motion trails obscuring play.

variants.name: Forsaken afterlife
variants.description: Cold light, still human figures, low mist and a distant red threshold.
variants.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: a new horror art-direction concept paintover of the user's actual first-person game screenshot, to compare in an art-style gallery.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, not a loose inspiration. Preserve the recognizable camera perspective, floor layout, large rectangular walls, receding freestanding bone arches, rib structure at far left, and recognizable skull-and-bone gun and wrapped arm at lower right. Landscape 16:9.
Primary direction: a frightening cinematic purgatorial afterlife, inspired by the oppressive cold practical lighting, ordinary places made uninhabitable, and uncanny human spirits of Insidious's The Further. Make an ORIGINAL environment and entities, not a recreation of movie characters or a movie screenshot.
Transform this from a brightly readable combat arena into a place where the dead silently wait. Physically plausible photographic materials, worn stained plaster and soot-dark metal, desiccated ivory bone, black stagnant atmosphere, old dark cloth. Existing walls partially lose their upper boundaries in darkness; the nearest two arches remain identifiable, the farther arch is swallowed by haze. No new elaborate cathedral, no architecture redesign.
LIGHT is the authored mechanism: a small hard cold blue-white light from near the player's position illuminates only the immediate floor, part of the closest arch and a pale face. Light falls away decisively. Dust and thin low ground mist have dimensional depth and gaps, not a uniform gray fog filter. Very sparse cyan-blue backscatter, mostly neutral blacks with dead desaturated brown-gray surfaces. A SINGLE distant muted deep red source barely contaminates the far doorway, not vivid neon strips. Turn OFF the continuous red floor grid glow and pink gun glow; the floor seams remain dark structural seams. Weapon is dimly visible by the near cold light, not spotlit as a product.
ENTITIES: replace the existing two obvious horned combat monsters with two horrifying almost-human adult dead figures in roughly their existing left and right middle-ground positions. NO HORNS, no armor, no fiery eyes. Left figure closer to the left wall wears decayed dark everyday clothing, stands utterly still with head slightly tilted, wax-pale skin, deep shadowed eye sockets, an unnaturally small frozen smile. Most of its lower body is lost in dark mist; only its face and one thin hand catch the light. Right figure stands deeper behind the existing wall edge, barely recognizable as a tall adult silhouette with a tiny strip of pale face, obscured rather than proudly displayed. Faces should be subtle and human enough to require a second look, not caricatures. NO additional foreground jump-scare face. No gore.
COMPOSITION: disturbing empty space dominates between player and entities. Keep enough local contrast to see the path and understand this is the same game. The result must be frightening through partial revelation, stillness and uncertain depth, not simply underexposed or blurred. Strong asymmetric visual tension within the original framing, filmic controlled grain, natural lens, restrained halation only around actual bright light. Surfaces realistically textured, NOT woodcut, NOT charcoal, NOT porcelain, not a painted illustration. Avoid epic spectacle, fantasy action posing, evenly spaced warm candles, bright arena fill, decorative gothic ornament, excessive chromatic aberration. No text, HUD, logos, borders, split view or watermark. Single full frame.
